chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, who transmitted it in mursal form, said:
Al-Jathaliq (the Catholicos) asked the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), saying: 'Inform me about God Almighty and Majestic — does He carry the Throne, or does the Throne carry Him?'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'God Almighty and Majestic is the Carrier of the Throne and the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them and between them. And that is the word of God Almighty and Majestic:
[Quran 35:41] Surely God upholds the heavens and the earth lest they fall apart; and if they were to fall apart, none could uphold them after Him — truly He is Forbearing, Forgiving.

He said: 'Then inform me about His word: [69:17] And above them eight shall bear the Throne of your Lord on that Day. How can He say that, when you said that He carries the Throne and the heavens and the earth?'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Throne — God the Exalted created it from four lights: a red light from which all redness became red, a green light from which all greenness became green, a yellow light from which all yellowness became yellow, and a white light from which all whiteness became white. And it is the Knowledge which God loaded upon the bearers, and that is a Light from His Magnificence.

By His Magnificence and His Light do the hearts of the believers see; by His Magnificence and His Light do the ignorant ones oppose Him; and by His Magnificence and His Light do all those in the heavens and the earth from all His creatures seek the means to Him through diverse deeds and varied religions.

Thus, every carried thing which God carries by His Light, Magnificence, and Power cannot of itself bring harm or benefit, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection. So everything is carried, and God Blessed and Exalted is the One Who upholds them both lest they fall apart, and Who encompasses them all, and He is the Life of everything and the Light of everything. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they say, with great exaltation.

He said to him: 'Then inform me about God Almighty and Majestic — where is He?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'He is here and here, above and below, surrounding us and with us, and it is His word:
[Quran 58:7] There is no secret counsel of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth, and not fewer than that nor more, but He is with them wherever they may be.

The Chair encompasses the heavens and the earth and what is between them and what is beneath the soil; and if you speak aloud, He knows the secret and what is more hidden. And that is the word of the Exalted:
[Quran 2:255] His Chair extends over the heavens and the earth, and preserving them both does not weary Him — He is the Most High, the Magnificent.

So those who bear the Throne — they are the scholars upon whom God has loaded His Knowledge. And nothing departs from these four things which God created in His Kingdom, which God showed to His elect and showed to His intimate friend (peace be upon him), and said:
[Quran 6:75] And thus We show Ibrahim the Kingdom of the heavens and the earth, so that he might be among those with certainty.
And how can the bearers of the Throne carry God, when by His Life their hearts came alive, and by His Light they were guided to His knowledge?

key_terms.الْجَاثَلِيق: Al-Jathaliq — the Catholicos (Patriarch of the Church of the East/Nestorian patriarch), representing Christian theological tradition
key_terms.الْحَمَلَة: The bearers — those entrusted to carry the Throne, identified here as the scholars of divine knowledge
key_terms.الْعَرْش: The Throne — the supreme symbol of God's sovereignty and power in Islamic cosmology
key_terms.الْكُرْسِيّ: The Chair/Footstool — interpreted in this hadith as representing God's encompassing knowledge
key_terms.الْمَلَكُوت: The Kingdom/Dominion — the spiritual realm of God's sovereignty
key_terms.الْمُرْسَل: Mursal — a hadith with a gap in the chain of transmission (rafa'ahu)
key_terms.الْوَسِيلَة: The means/medium — the way of drawing near to God through acts of worship
key_terms.حَامِل: The Carrier/Upholder — one who bears and sustains

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the Throne of God and who truly bears it?
ai.summary: This hadith records a theological dialogue between al-Jathaliq (the Catholicos or Catholic Patriarch, likely the Patriarch of the East) and Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) concerning the nature of the Divine Throne (al-'Arsh) and Chair (al-Kursi). Imam Ali's response resolves the apparent contradiction between God's ontological self-sufficiency (nothing truly carries God, for He upholds all things) and the Quranic reference to eight bearers of the Throne, by explaining that the Throne is created from four divine lights representing God's Knowledge, and the true 'bearers of the Throne' are the scholars upon whom God has loaded that Knowledge. The dialogue illustrates the Imam's mastery of speculative theology (kalam) in engaging Christian interlocutors, demonstrating that divine transcendence and omnipresence are not contradictory — God encompasses all, and the Kursi (Chair/Footstool) is His encompassing knowledge, not a physical location.
